title: The Friday surah
hookLine: many read al-Kahf every Friday, a practice drawn from hadith (Hakim; Bayhaqi)
tomorrow: The young men in the cave

cards: A Friday morning, a mosque, an hour before the noon prayer. Along the walls, people sit alone, each with a Qur'an open to the same place. Ask one of them and you may hear: it's Friday, so it's al-Kahf.
Surah eighteen, The Cave: a surah with a weekly appointment. Some read it in Arabic, some in translation, some under their breath. Today: where that appointment comes from.

teach.h: A LIGHT BETWEEN THE TWO FRIDAYS.
teach.b: The custom rests on a hadith recorded by al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi: whoever reads Surat al-Kahf on Friday, a light will shine for them between the two Fridays.
Hadith scholars have discussed how strong its chains are, and the practice has lasted. Because the Islamic day begins at sunset, some read it on Thursday night, others on Friday itself.
Another hadith, in Sahih Muslim, says that whoever memorizes the first ten verses of al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal, the great deceiver of the end of time.
That's one reason some families teach those verses early.
And Bukhari tells a scene: a companion was reciting al-Kahf at night, his horse tied nearby, when a cloud came down over him and began to circle, and the horse grew restless.
In the morning he told the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, who said: that was the sakinah, the tranquility, which came down for the Qur'an.
The surah opens, in Pickthall's words: "Praise be to Allah Who hath revealed the Scripture unto His slave, and hath not placed therein any crookedness".
Then come four long stories: young men who hide in a cave, a man with two gardens, Musa traveling to learn from a stranger, and a powerful traveler who builds a wall.
Some teachers today read them as four trials: of faith, wealth, knowledge and power.
That framing is a modern reading, not a hadith, but it helps hold the surah in your head. This week, one story at a time.

how: Many Muslims read Surat al-Kahf every Friday, or from Thursday sunset, alone or in groups at the mosque; some also memorize its first ten verses, following the hadith in Sahih Muslim.

games.q: you're reciting al-Kahf at night and a cloud comes down and circles you; your horse won't settle. you tell the Prophet in the morning. what does he say?
o: it was a bad sign; stop reciting at night.
it was the sakinah, coming down for the Qur'an.
games.why: the sakinah, tranquility, came down for the Qur'an (Bukhari).

practice: Think through your coming Friday and find a half hour that could belong to al-Kahf: before work, at lunch, after the noon prayer, on the train.
If the whole surah feels like a lot, picture just the first ten verses, in Arabic or in translation, and where you'd sit to read them. If you pray, you can ask for that week of light.
